correctness.rationale: For six shattered KG(13,3) support triples, singleton hit traces force six distinct private coordinates; the empty trace requires three unused coordinates; hence the residual two-element edges span ≤4 coordinates. With ≤3 residual coordinates, a four-hit trace avoiding two residual edges cannot be realized by a three-point center. With exactly four, any two residual edges must intersect or a four-hit trace is impossible. A pairwise-intersecting 2-edge multigraph spanning four vertices is a common-center star, with arm multiplicities m1+m2+m3=6. Omitting one support from each of two arms forces each remaining arm multiplicity ≥2, giving (2,2,2). Conversely each hit trace uses at most one coordinate per arm and pads with three unused, proving shattering. Orbit-stabilizer gives 13!/288=21,621,600 unordered six-supports and unique orbit. Independently enumerated all 286 three-point centers for canonical support to verify all 64 traces; also recomputed count 13*C(12,3)*C(9,6)*90.
